title: ISO 9001 QMS
description: A quality management system on the ISO 9001:2026 requirement library: context, quality policy and objectives, processes, risks and opportunities, controlled documents, nonconformities with corrective actions and customer feedback; Full adds external providers, competence, measuring equipment, internal audits, management review, design and development and release records. Example items start with "Example:".

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: The core of a QMS: context and interested parties, quality policy and objectives, processes, risks and opportunities, quality documents, nonconformities and corrective action, customer feedback and complaints.

levels.name: Full
levels.description: Everything in Starter plus external providers, competence and training, measuring equipment, internal audits with findings, management review, design and development and release records.

sheets.name: Context and interested parties
sheets.description: What shapes your quality management system: the internal and external issues that affect what you deliver, the interested parties and what they need from you, and the scope statement with any requirement you say does not apply and why. Link each entry to the clause it answers.

fields.name: Clause
fields.description: The clause this entry answers: 4.1 for issues, 4.2 for interested parties, 4.3 for the scope.

fields.name: Their requirements
fields.description: What this party expects from you, and which of those expectations the quality system takes on.

items.name: Example: customers expect shorter lead times

values.details: Two large customers moved to weekly call-offs. Late deliveries now cost us orders.
values.response: On-time delivery is a quality objective and part of the order to delivery process.

items.name: Example: key know-how sits with a few experienced people

values.details: Three long-serving technicians do most of the set-ups. Two retire within three years.

values.needs: Products that meet the agreed specification, delivered on the agreed date, and a quick answer when something goes wrong.

values.details: Write which products and services, sites and processes the quality system covers. Name any requirement that does not apply (often design and development) and why it does not affect conformity or customer satisfaction.

sheets.name: Quality policy and objectives
sheets.description: The commitments of your quality policy and the measurable objectives that follow from them: how each is measured, the target, where you are now, who owns it and the plan to get there. Review each one on its date.

fields.name: How it is measured
fields.description: The measure (KPI) and where the number comes from.

fields.name: Lower is better
fields.description: Tick when a smaller number is the goal, for example complaints per month.

config.expr: IF(OR(EMPTY({target}), EMPTY({actual})), "", IF({lower_better} = "Yes", IF({actual} <= {target}, "Met", "Not met"), IF({actual} >= {target}, "Met", "Not met")))

fields.name: Plan to achieve it
fields.description: What will be done, the resources it needs, who is responsible and by when.

rules.message: Say why this objective is retired.

items.name: Example: we deliver what we promised, when we promised it

values.plan: Write each commitment of the quality policy as its own entry, so objectives can be traced back to it.

items.name: Example: on-time delivery of at least 95 %

values.measure: Orders shipped on or before the confirmed date, per month, from the order system
values.plan: Weekly capacity check in the planning meeting; confirm dates only after the check.

items.name: Example: no more than 2 customer complaints a month

values.measure: Complaints logged in Customer feedback and complaints, per month

sheets.name: Processes
sheets.description: The processes your quality system needs and how they work together: what goes in and comes out, who owns each one, how you know it works (its measures) and the risks that could stop it.

fields.name: Inputs
fields.description: What starts the process and what it needs, and where it comes from.

fields.name: Outputs
fields.description: What the process delivers, and to whom.

fields.name: Measures (KPIs)
fields.description: How you know the process works: the measures, their targets and how often you check them.

values.inputs: Customer orders and call-offs; confirmed specifications; stock and capacity.
values.outputs: Products delivered to the agreed specification and date; invoices.
values.kpis: On-time delivery (monthly, target 95 %); orders entered without error (monthly, target 99 %).

values.inputs: Purchase requests; the approved supplier list.
values.outputs: Purchase orders with clear requirements; goods checked at receipt.
values.kpis: Supplier on-time delivery (monthly); goods rejected at receipt (monthly).

sheets.name: Risks and opportunities
sheets.description: Risks that could stop you delivering conforming products and services or satisfied customers, and opportunities to do better: each with an owner, a score, the action you take and whether it worked.

fields.name: Details
fields.description: What could happen, why, and what it would mean for customers or products.

fields.name: Likelihood
fields.description: 1 rare, 5 almost certain.

fields.name: Impact
fields.description: 1 hardly noticed, 5 lost customers or unsafe product. For an opportunity: the benefit.

fields.name: Action
fields.description: What you do about it, built into the process where you can.

fields.name: Did it work?
fields.description: How you checked that the action had the effect you wanted.

rules.message: Add the action and how you checked that it worked before closing.

items.name: Example: orders confirmed beyond our capacity

values.details: Sales confirms dates without checking the plan; late deliveries follow in busy months.
values.action: Confirm delivery dates only after the weekly capacity check.

items.name: Example: one supplier for a critical component

values.details: The control board comes from one supplier. A stoppage there stops our line within two weeks.
values.action: Qualify a second source and hold four weeks of safety stock.

items.name: Example: customers order through a web portal

values.details: Fewer order entry errors and faster confirmations.

sheets.name: Quality documents
sheets.description: The documented information your quality system keeps: what you maintain (policy, scope, procedures, instructions) and what you retain as records. Controlled documents: approved by a second person, reviewed on a date. Attach the files on each document's Files tab.

rules.message: Add a version note: what changed in this version.
Say why this approved document changes status.

items.name: Approved external providers and their evaluations

sheets.name: Nonconformities and corrective action
sheets.description: Anything that did not meet a requirement: a complaint, an audit finding, a supplier problem, a nonconforming product. Record what you did with the affected output, the correction, the root cause, the corrective actions (as sub-items) and the check that they worked. A nonconformity closes only when its actions are done.

fields.name: What happened to the output
fields.description: How the nonconforming product or service was dealt with, and who authorised it.

fields.name: Correction
fields.description: What was done straight away to contain it and limit the effect.

fields.name: Corrective action
fields.description: What removes the cause so it does not happen again. Track the steps as sub-items.

lines.text: It has not happened again since
Risks, processes and documents are updated where needed

rules.message: Add the root cause, the corrective action and the effectiveness check before closing.
Say why this does not apply.

items.name: Example: wrong labels on a delivery to a customer

values.description: Labels showed last year's part number. The customer held the goods at receipt.
values.correction: Relabelled at the customer's site within two days.

layout.title: Report a nonconformity
layout.description: Tell us when something does not meet a requirement: a faulty product, a step in a process that was skipped, a supplier delivery that is wrong, a promise to a customer that was not kept. Report it even when you have already fixed it.
layout.nameLabel: What is wrong, in one line

fields.label: What is wrong
fields.help: What you saw, where and when, and how you noticed it.

fields.label: Which product, service or process is affected?
What have you done about it so far?
fields.help: For example: stopped the line, put the parts aside, told the customer. Write "Nothing yet" if so.

fields.label: How serious do you think it is?
fields.help: Your best guess. The owner decides.

fields.label: Your name
fields.help: So the owner can ask you more.

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The quality team has your report and will contact you if they need more.

notice.purpose: To record and correct nonconformities and stop them happening again.
notice.recipients: The people in this workspace who handle nonconformities and corrective action.
notice.retention: Kept for 3 years after the nonconformity is closed.
notice.rights: You can ask to see, correct or delete what you reported. Contact the person who shared this form.

sheets.name: Customer feedback and complaints
sheets.description: What customers tell you: complaints, praise, suggestions and survey results. Log each complaint through the form "Report a complaint" (Forms tab), answer the customer and tick Needs corrective action when the cause must be fixed for good: that raises a nonconformity.

fields.name: Needs corrective action
fields.description: Tick when the cause must be found and fixed for good: a nonconformity is raised and linked.

rules.message: Add the answer you gave the customer before closing.

items.name: Example: delivery arrived a week late

values.description: The goods came seven days after the confirmed date and the customer's line stood still for a day.

items.name: Example: wrong labels on a delivery

values.description: Labels showed an old part number, so goods receipt held the delivery.
values.response: Apologised, relabelled on site within two days and raised a corrective action.

values.description: 38 customers answered. Lowest marks for delivery reliability, highest for technical support.
values.response: Delivery reliability is a quality objective for next year.

layout.title: Report a complaint
layout.description: Log a complaint as soon as a customer raises it, however small, by email, on the phone or in person. Write down what the customer said, in their words where you can.

fields.label: Customer contact
fields.help: An email address so the handler can answer them.

fields.label: Which product, order or service is it about?
How serious is it for the customer?
fields.help: Your best guess. The handler decides.

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The complaint is logged and the handler will answer the customer.

notice.purpose: To handle customer complaints, answer the customer and improve our products and services.
notice.recipients: The people in this workspace who handle customer complaints.
notice.retention: Kept for 3 years after the complaint is closed.
notice.rights: You and the customer can ask to see, correct or delete what was recorded. Contact the person who shared this form.

sheets.name: External providers
sheets.description: The suppliers and subcontractors whose products, services or outsourced processes affect what you deliver: the criteria you choose them by, each evaluation and when they are evaluated again.

fields.name: Evaluation criteria
fields.description: What you judge them on: quality, delivery, price, certification, responsiveness.

rules.message: Add the criteria, the evaluation date and the next evaluation before approving.

values.provides: Assembled control boards to our drawing.
values.criteria: Rejects at receipt under 0.5 %, on-time delivery over 95 %, ISO 9001 certificate valid.

values.provides: Calibration of our gauges and torque tools, traceable to national standards.

sheets.name: Competence and training
sheets.description: The competence each role needs for work that affects quality, what you do to close a gap (training, coaching, hiring), the record that it was done and whether it worked.

fields.name: Was it effective?
fields.description: How you checked that the person can now do the work.

items.name: Example: machine set-up for a new operator

values.competence: Sets up the press for every product family without help
Knows the quality policy, their objectives and what happens when work does not conform

sheets.name: Measuring equipment
sheets.description: The gauges, instruments and test equipment you rely on to show products conform: each with an ID, its calibration interval, the last result and the next due date. Equipment found out of calibration needs a check of what it measured since its last good calibration.

fields.name: If found out of tolerance
fields.description: What was measured since the last good calibration, whether it was still valid, and what you did.

rules.message: Add the calibration date and the next due date.

sheets.name: Internal audit programme
sheets.description: The internal audits you plan and run over the cycle, weighted by how important and how risky each process is and by earlier results: the processes and clauses each covers, who leads it (never their own work) and what it found.

items.name: Example: purchasing and order to delivery

values.scope: The purchasing and order to delivery processes against our procedures and the clauses in scope.

sheets.name: Audit findings
sheets.description: What each internal audit found. A finding of type Nonconformity raises an item in Nonconformities and corrective action and links to it.

fields.name: Grade
fields.description: Major: the requirement is not met at all, or the system cannot be relied on there. Minor: a single lapse.

fields.name: What was found
fields.description: The requirement, what you saw and the evidence for it.

items.name: Example: supplier re-evaluations not done on time

values.details: Two of eight approved suppliers sampled were past their re-evaluation date.

sheets.name: Management review
sheets.description: Top management's reviews of the quality system at planned intervals: tick the inputs you covered and record the decisions on improvements, changes and resources.

fields.name: Decisions and outputs
fields.description: Improvements, changes to the quality system and resources needed.

rules.message: Add the meeting date and the decisions.

sheets.name: Design and development
sheets.description: Only when you design products or services yourself. Each project from plan to release: the inputs, the reviews, verification and validation, and changes. If you do not design, leave this sheet empty or archive it, and say why in the scope statement.

fields.name: Design inputs
fields.description: Functional and performance needs, legal requirements, lessons from earlier designs.

fields.name: Design outputs
fields.description: Drawings, specifications and acceptance criteria that production and release use.

fields.name: Verified
fields.description: The outputs meet the inputs.

fields.name: Validated
fields.description: The product or service works for its intended use.

fields.name: Changes after release of the design

rules.message: Record the inputs and outputs and tick verified and validated before release.

sheets.name: Release records
sheets.description: Evidence that each product batch or service was checked against its acceptance criteria before it went to the customer, and who released it. A failed check is a nonconformity.

rules.message: Add the criteria, who released it and when.

values.criteria: Dimensions to drawing rev C on 5 samples; visual check of all parts; certificate of conformity attached.

setup.title: ISO 9001 setup
setup.description: Eight steps from an empty quality system to one you can audit. Each step's progress comes from your sheets.

steps.title: Define your context and scope
steps.body: Write down the issues that affect what you deliver, who expects what from you and what the quality system covers. Mark each ISO 9001 requirement applicable or not, with a reason.

steps.title: Set the quality policy and objectives
steps.body: Agree the commitments of your quality policy, then set at least three objectives, each with a measure, a target and an owner.

steps.title: Map your processes and their risks
steps.body: Name the processes you need, with an owner, their inputs and outputs and how you measure them. Note the risks and opportunities that matter and what you do about each.

steps.title: Write and approve your documents
steps.body: Write the documents you need, attach each on the Files tab and have someone other than the author approve it. Approved documents get a review date.

steps.title: Make complaints easy to log
steps.body: Open the form "Report a complaint", check its questions and privacy notice, then open it and tell everyone who talks to customers where to find it. Answer and close your first complaint.

steps.title: Evaluate your external providers
steps.body: List the suppliers and subcontractors that affect what you deliver, evaluate each against your criteria and set the date of the next evaluation.

starter.body: Starter has no supplier sheet: keep the list of approved external providers with their evaluations and approve it as a record in Quality documents.

steps.title: Run an internal audit
steps.body: Plan audits that cover every process over the cycle, run them with someone independent of the work, record what they find and raise nonconformities for what falls short.

starter.body: Starter has no audit programme: run the audit, approve its report as the internal audit record in Quality documents and record each shortfall in Nonconformities and corrective action with the source Internal audit.

steps.title: Hold a management review
steps.body: Bring top management together to look at how the quality system performs, cover every input and record the decisions they take.

starter.body: Starter has no meeting sheet: hold the review, write the minutes and approve them as the management review record in Quality documents.
